Human evaluation remains the gold standard ... We conducted two distinct human evaluation studies to validate our approach: (1) an assessment of our automated checklist generation process, and (2) a direct comparison between LLM and human scores using the CheckEval protocol.
We recruited three human evaluators with Ph.D. student-level qualifications or above in Computer Science, all of whom had a background in evaluation research and summarization/dialogue tasks.
guideline: Annotators scored augmented/filtered questions; manually applied checklist with ~25 binary questions per dimension
Human annotators were given the same checklist questions and asked to answer yes/no for each criterion; they also rated summaries and dialogue responses on the predefined dimensions.
Each evaluation dimension was first decomposed into finer-grained sub-dimensions, and a set of seed questions was written to cover each sub-dimension.
